name: Cheltenham Half Marathon
notes: The A race. Target 1:21-1:23, model predicts 1:22:23. COURSE (from a clubmate's 2025 file — her run, not his — who ran 1:21:02, so her splits map the course at almost exactly his goal pace): 101m gain over 21.09km, ~4.8m/km, rolling rather than flat, net slightly downhill start to finish. Her watch had no barometric altimeter, so treat the metres as approximate and the shape as the signal. Km 1 is downhill and her fastest of the day (3:38) — the start is a trap. Highest ground is the first 8km, which roll continuously. Flattest running is roughly 14-18km. The sting is km 19-20: a climb of about 11m that produced her slowest split of the race (4:11, seven seconds off anything else), immediately followed by a 6m drop to the line where she ran 3:54. Expect the 20km split to look bad and the last km to be free. HER PACING IS THE WARNING: first 10km 37:08 (3:43/km), second 10km 39:33 (3:57/km) — 2:25 lost in the back half after going out 7 sec/km faster than her own average. 3:43/km is Shep's current 10K race pace, so running with that early group means racing a half at 10K pace.

name: Sharpness 4
notes: CONFIRMED 28 Sep: Crete is off and this replaces it. Road, 4 miles. HE FRAMES IT AS AN INTERESTING CHALLENGE, NOT A TARGET - keep it that way: no taper, no recovery week after. Club record reads '23:3' on the list, so 23:30-23:39; 23:30 needs 3:39/km average, 23:39 needs 3:40/km. COURSE (from a clubmate's file, 28 Sep - her run, not his; the same clubmate whose 1:21:02 Cheltenham file mapped that course): rolling but gentle. Her watch said ~51 m of climbing, but it lacks a barometric altimeter; his Google Maps route of the loop (30 Sep) gives ~33 m up and ~36 m down, 12-31 m elevation range, 'mostly flat' - map elevation is the better number, so her 51 m was GPS noise inflating it. The loop: start at the Old Docks, Dock Road, south to Newtown, east to Victoria Place, north through Brookend and Old Brookend, then back west through Sharpness and down to the docks. High ground is about three-quarters of the way round, then a downhill finish. Km 1 is downhill then flat - she ran it 3:32 at HR 159, the fastest full km of her race: the same trap as Cheltenham's km 1. First climb to ~2 km (+13 m, her 3:43). Km 3 drops then starts rising (3:33). A long drag from 3 km to about 4.3 km (3:46). Km 5 dips (3:42). The crux is km 6: two short steep ramps around 5.1-5.7 km, her slowest by ten seconds (3:56). Then a downhill last ~0.4 km (3:31). Her HR sat at 172 from km 2 to the line - she was at her ceiling from the first hill. HER TIME, about 23:40 (23:36-23:44 depending on the final segment's true length), still calibrates - she ran 1:21:02 at Cheltenham against his 1:21:03 - but with the course gentler than her watch implied, the ~38 s between her time and the 23:02 flat Riegel off Cheltenham is mostly about her day rather than the hills, so it says less about the course than first read. Working estimate from the blended flat projection (23:17-23:20): add roughly 5-15 s for two weeks without quality since a maximal half, and roughly 5-15 s for ~33 m of rolling climb, giving about 23:30-23:50. Against a 23:30-23:39 record that is possible on a good day and a coin flip, not a likely miss - slightly better than the 23:35-23:55 read of 28 Sep, which leaned on her watch's 51 m. When she ran it, and at what fitness, is still unknown. PACING: even effort, not even pace. Do not copy her 3:32 opening; about 3:38. Let the climbs at 2 km and 3-4.3 km cost a few seconds by effort, take the descents, expect km 6 to be the slowest split and do not chase it, then use the downhill finish. Week before, race-day protocol and aftermath as in the 27 Sep proposal: one short 200 m session midweek, strides Friday, no heavy legs after Thursday, 3 km warm-up, Symbicort 20 min / salbutamol 15 min, Puma Fast-R Nitro 3, 2-3 easy days after then straight into the Guy Fawkes block.

name: Stroud 10K
notes: Added 4 Oct: a free place in his home town, and HE IS RACING IT. Entry confirmed 6 Oct: the 10K showed as fully booked on 5 Oct, but he got a place after all, so it stands as the target. This is now the target race of the October block, with Guy Fawkes 5 a week later demoted to an experiment. Why the 10K leads: his only 2026 10K is June's 38:06, untapered, so a fresh 10K is the best evidence the predictor can get for Manchester - far more than another 5-miler. Current projection (weighted predictor, 4 Oct): 37:20. COURSE (from a Strava file he sent 6 Oct - whose run and which year not yet confirmed; max HR 197 suggests not his): gentler than 'Stroud is hilly' implied. 60 m gain, elevation range ~23-50 m, but NET UPHILL ~+15 m (start ~34 m, finish ~50 m), with the climbing loaded into the back half. Per-km elevation: 1 -11, 2 +12, 3 -4, 4 +2, 5 -3, 6 +1, 7 +4, 8 +5, 9 -2, 10 +10. Shape: downhill start to the low point ~0.8 km, climb to ~36 m at 2 km, rolling 26-35 m from 2 to 6.3 km, then a steady drag from ~6.3 to 8.4 km (30 to 41 m), a dip and roll through km 9, and a sharp climb over the last ~600 m to the finish (~37 to 50 m). NO FREE LAST KM - unlike Cheltenham and Sharpness the finish is uphill. THAT RUNNER'S SPLITS (~39:00): 3:53, 3:55, 3:56, 3:55, 4:02, 4:03, 4:00, 3:48, 3:46, 3:41 - a fade over km 5-7 with HR jumping 170 to 184, then a strong rally up the back-half climbs. Course cost vs flat: ~15-25 s by grade-adjusted maths (about 0.7 s per metre climbed at his pace, ~0.4 s back per metre descended). The Sharpness lesson says use the low end. So ~37:35-37:45 off the 37:20 flat projection; sub-38 is the realistic target, high 37:20s-30s on a good day. PACING (even effort, ~3:45 average, ~37:35): km1 3:40-3:42 (downhill start - the same trap as Cheltenham and Sharpness, do not take the whole gift); km2 ~3:50 (the first climb, by effort); km3-6 3:43-3:45 (rolling - this is where the other runner faded, so concentration rather than pace); km7-8 3:47-3:48 (the long drag, give time by effort); km9 3:42-3:44 (the dip); km10 3:48-3:50 (the finishing climb - kick only once over the top, if at all). RACE WEEK (19-25 Oct) replaces what the 4 Oct proposal wrote provisionally: the 24 Oct 2x2-mile session goes - nothing hard inside ~3 days of the race; Wed 21 Oct 6x600m stays as the last sharpener (4 days out); Thu-Fri easy, strides Fri; Sat 24 Oct easy 30-35 min shakeout, no strides; Sun 25 Oct race, ~16 km all in with 3 km warm-up and cool-down (principle 6). No heavy leg session after Wed 21 Oct. Race protocol: Symbicort 20 min, salbutamol 15 min before, Puma Fast-R Nitro 3.

name: Guy Fawkes 5
notes: DEMOTED 4 Oct TO AN EXPERIMENT, his word: the Stroud 10K a week earlier (25 Oct) is now the target, and he has the Linda Frank 5 in January as the next shot at this distance. Club record 29:12. Projection off the weighted predictor (4 Oct) is 29:40, so the record was already a stretch on a fresh week; a hard 10K seven days before costs more - my estimate 10-20 s, and the evidence on a seven-day turnaround at 50 is thin, so treat that as a guess. The experiment is how he races a 5-mile a week after a 10K. The week between is genuinely easy: Monday rest, easy running, strides Thursday, nothing hard, no heavy legs. Race it as he feels on the day - not a record attempt unless the legs say so.

name: Boddington 10
notes: Club record up for grabs at 1:01:00. Course confirmed flat, so Riegel holds without a downward adjustment. TWO PROJECTIONS: off Cheltenham alone (1:21:03) 1:00:50, ten seconds inside; off race_prediction.json's four-race blend 1:01:38, 38 seconds short. The blend is the planning number. Either way this is closer than it was in September, and it has four months of marathon base-building in front of it — the aerobic work for Manchester is exactly the work that moves a 10-mile time. Falls mid-way through that build, so it needs a short taper written into the block rather than being run off unbroken loading.

name: Fission 20
notes: Added 6 Oct as possible, his suggestion. Flat 20 miles from the decommissioned Berkeley Power Station (GL13 9PA), Rogue Runs, with a half option on the same day. ENTRY: last year's opened 1 Nov and it has sold out every year - 1 Nov 2026 is Guy Fawkes morning, so remind him before then. WHY IT FITS: 4-5 weeks before Manchester, it is the 32 km long run the winter build already has around 21 Mar, but with drink stations, a race-morning routine, race shoes and a crowd - the untested parts of a first marathon. RUN IT AS A REHEARSAL, NOT A RACE: first 10 miles steady ~4:30/km, last 10 miles at goal MP 4:16/km, carbohydrate 60-90 g/h from ~20 min (the brief's fuelling table), nothing new on the day. Racing 20 miles flat out at 50 costs 2-3 weeks of recovery that a 4-week-out race cannot spare. CLUB RECORD 2:23:06 (4:27/km): that pacing comes out at ~2:21, so the record falls as a by-product of the rehearsal without racing it. Keep it that way - if the day is warm, windy or HRV is down, the rehearsal still stands and the record is dropped, never the other way round. Even-paced alternative ~4:24/km gives ~2:22. THE HALF OPTION: flat and fast, tempting for the 1:20:46 PB, but he cannot do both on one day and the 20 is worth more for a first marathon - look for a separate half in late Feb (~7 weeks out) for the PB.

name: Manchester Marathon
notes: Goal sub-3 (4:16/km). Volume, not fitness, is the binding constraint, and Cheltenham widened the margin rather than closing a gap: race_prediction.json now projects 2:51:16 off four blended races (2:49 off Cheltenham alone), against 2:52 before the race. The fitness is comfortably there on paper. What is missing is that he has never run one, his longest run ever is ~29 km, and carbohydrate at marathon pace in marathon quantity is untested.
